info.bio: The Cult es una banda inglesa de Hard rock y Rock gótico. A mediados de los 80's, The Cult fue una de las principales bandas que hicieron resurgir el Hard rock en Inglaterra; una banda de rock con algunos toques Psicodélicos, influenciados principalmente por el misticismo de The Doors y el estilo de las guitarras de hard rock de Led Zeppelin y AC/DC. La banda comenzó con un estilo rock gótico post-punk[1] , y fue evolucionando hacia el Hard rock a partir del disco "Electric" (1987).

scenes.name: Gótico
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Término que Hannett aplicó a Joy Division y luego insulto para los epígonos, hasta que en 1982 los fans lo adoptan como estandarte frente a la excesiva luminosidad del new pop: glamour sepulcral, retorno de lo reprimido, emociones atemporales. Bauhaus («Bela Lugosi's Dead», 1979, el comienzo propiamente dicho; Peter Murphy, sex symbol heredero de Adam Ant y Bowie), The Birthday Party (el gótico americano de Nick Cave: «Release the Bats», Junkyard), Killing Joke («música de tensión», del funk de PiL a Black Sabbath, con un aura inquietante), The Cure (gótico light: Seventeen Seconds, Faith, Pornography). El club The Batcave (1982), el «positive punk», Southern Death Cult, Theatre of Hate, The Sisters of Mercy («¡Nosotros sí somos una banda de rock!»), el death rock de Los Ángeles y Kukl con Björk. Su deriva: coqueteos totalitarios y la conversión en versión postpunk del heavy metal (The Cult).

scenes.name: Indie, C86 y el giro retro
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En 1985 la energía se ha disipado: el new pop cae en la decadencia (Live Aid, «una tragedia para el pop»), los singles independientes venden la mitad que en 1980 y «independiente» se convierte en «indie», un género de guitarras sucias, voces pálidas y nostalgia de los sesenta, oposición impotente al mainstream. El futurismo da paso al «rock de coleccionista»: The Jesus and Mary Chain (Psychocandy: Ronettes y Beach Boys con feedback), el sello Creation y Primal Scream, la cassette C86 de NME (The Pastels, Shop Assistants, The Soup Dragons, June Brides) y su culto a la inocencia, que reaparecerá en el riot grrrl. The Smiths y R.E.M., contra los ochenta; Hüsker Dü, Sonic Youth, Butthole Surfers y Dinosaur Jr. redescubren el acid rock; de ahí, Nirvana.

scenes.name: Dark punk y rock gótico
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk británico estuvo flanqueado desde el principio por un movimiento «gótico» que canalizaba su violencia hacia atmósferas de terror y rituales esotéricos: Stranglers, Siouxsie, X-Ray Spex. Lo más interesante evita el tono de película de terror: The Cure introducen la angustia existencial de Camus y Sartre (Pornography, Disintegration); Joy Division mezclan Doors, Kraftwerk y Black Sabbath y su final anuncia el synth-pop; Bauhaus, Killing Joke, Psychedelic Furs, los irlandeses Virgin Prunes y la cima del género, Public Image Ltd de Johnny Lydon, que convierte el punk en música de cámara con dub y ecos étnicos (Second Edition, Flowers Of Romance). Después, el gótico bailable de Sisters Of Mercy, Alien Sex Fiend, Cult, Mission e In The Nursery.

podcast.title: 12-inch Remix Business
podcast.body: The Cult was among the bands that engaged in the 12-inch remix trend, following the influence of New Order's "Blue Monday." This format became a key element of club culture and alternative music in the 1980s. "And so was Depeche Mode and The Cure and The Human League and Simple Minds and The Cult and Killing Joke and Erasure and Psychedelic Furs and Madness. They all got into the 12-inch business."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band Name Evolution
podcast.body: Before settling on "The Cult," the band went by two other names: Southern Death Cult (for one album) and Death Cult (for another). By the end of 1983, they were simply "The Cult." "Up until that record came out, The Cult went by two other names."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The Cult is listed among Bob Rock's clients. "We got the cult, Veruch assault, Erasmith, Motley crew, Ardady Pease, the Tea Party, Eric and High Fy, Afghan Wigs, David Lee Roth, the Conorline Crush, Cher."

podcast.title: Formed by Billy Duffy
podcast.body: Guitarist Billy Duffy formed The Cult with Ian Astbury a couple of years after his brief tenure in The Nosebleeds with Morrissey. "Billy going on to form the cult with Ian Aspery a couple of years later."

podcast.title: Later Commercial Success
podcast.body: After their evolution from Southern Death Cult and Death Cult, The Cult achieved significant commercial success, selling millions of records in the late 1980s and early 1990s. "And yes, it is the cult that went on to sell millions of records in the late 80s and early 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mark Brachecki as Video Drummer
podcast.body: The drummer seen in the music video for "She Sells Sanctuary" was Mark Brachecki, who was on loan from the band Big Country, as Nigel Preston had already been fired. "The drummer we see in the video for Sanctuary is a dude named Mark Brachecki, who was on loan from the band Big Country."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Nigel Preston's Drinking Problem
podcast.body: Drummer Nigel Preston had a serious drinking problem that made him increasingly unreliable during recording sessions, often showing up late or too drunk to play. This unreliability directly led to the minimalist drumming on "She Sells Sanctuary." "Nigel however had a serious drinking problem and was becoming more and more unreliable."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Nigel Preston's Firing and Death
podcast.body: Although "Sanctuary" and the "Love" album were major hits, Nigel Preston was fired shortly after his parts were recorded due to his unreliability. He later died in 1992, but his drumming on "She Sells Sanctuary" remains a part of The Cult's legacy. "Nigel wasn't invited to stick around. He was fired soon after all his parts were recorded."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.body: An Ian Astbury-led band mentioned as one of the many groups contributing to the expanding goth scene in the 1983-1984 period. It later evolved into Death Cult and then The Cult. "In Asperg band, Southern Death Cult."

xref.title: Jazz Coleman's Disappearance (2012)
xref.body: In July 2012, Jazz Coleman unexpectedly disappeared. He appeared to be upset about Killing Joke's impending tour with The Cult and expressed a strong desire to dissociate himself from both the tour and the band, which was publicly voiced in a scathing Facebook post. Approximately a month later, he was located living a "nomadic existence" in the Western Sahara. Coleman subsequently claimed that the controversial Facebook post was not authored by him but by an imposter. "Jazz seemed angry that killing joke was going on tour with the cult, and he didn't want to have anything to do with the road trip or the band."

xref.title: Battle of Bands Win Led to Bob Rock's First Ever Production Credit
xref.body: The band started as the K-Tels in 1978 in Vancouver but were threatened with legal action by the cheap record company K-tel International and renamed themselves Young Canadians. Frontman Art Bergman would remain a presence in Canadian alt-rock for decades, ultimately being made a Member of the Order of Canada in 2020. The band won a local Battle of the Bands contest that awarded them studio time at a new facility called Little Mountain Sound. The engineer assigned to these unknown contest winners was a young man named Bob Rock — it was the first time Rock ever produced anything. He went on to produce Metallica, Mötley Crüe, Bon Jovi, The Cult, the Tragically Hip, and many others. "The engineer assigned to them was some kid named Bob Rock."

xref.title: Second Generation Goth Influence
xref.body: Along with The Cure, The Sisters of Mercy, Siouxsie and the Banshees, and Joy Division, Bauhaus records were a significant part of "second generation Goth" in the latter half of the 1980s. "Along with the cure and the sister of mercy, choosing the banshees and some immortal Bauhaus and joy division records, there were a series of other bands that, well not exactly big in the mainstream, were huge parts of the cult of the Goth."

xref.title: Solo Career Trajectory
xref.body: After The Smiths' breakup, Morrissey initially seemed poised to become a major solo star, benefiting from the cult following he amassed with his previous band. However, his solo career began to decline in the mid-1990s, as he struggled to produce consistent albums, moved to Los Angeles, refused interviews, and toured less frequently. "Although it got off to a promising start, Morris' solo career hit the skids in the mid 1990s."
